clips.name: tee shots
clips.prompt: Close-up, camera on a tripod right beside a disc golf tee pad in a quiet wooded park. A player's arm swings through and rips a backhand throw: the plastic disc snaps out of the hand and whooshes fast past the camera lens, spinning away down the fairway. He throws three discs in a row, a few seconds apart, each one a sharp, airy, spinning whoosh that fades into the distance. Realistic, crisp, close-miked sound only: the swish of the arm, the snap of the release and the disc's whoosh. No music, no voices, no birds, no wind.

clips.name: landings
clips.prompt: Locked-off camera at ground level beside a short-mown grass fairway in a quiet park on a calm sunny afternoon. A red plastic disc golf disc flies in fast and low from the left, spinning, cutting through the air right past the camera, then hits the grass, skids a short way and wobbles flat to a stop. A second later a blue disc does the same on a hard packed dirt path in the foreground. Realistic, crisp sound only: the airy spinning whoosh of each disc as it passes the microphone and the dull thump, brushing slide and little wobble as it lands. No music, no voices, no wind noise, no birds.
clips.takes: python3 tools/process-sfx.py land_grass landing.wav --peak -6 --at 1.92-2.95,1.94-2.5 && python3 tools/process-sfx.py land_dirt landing.wav --peak -6 --at 5.93-6.95,7.3-7.98

runtime: src/audio.js: whoosh on release (gain and pitch follow power), land_grass / land_dirt on first ground contact by surface (gain follows impact speed); a random take each time, synthesis as the fallback.

local.tool: Stable Audio 3 small, run locally in ComfyUI (C:\ComfyUI) on the owner's RTX 5090: CheckpointLoaderSimple stable_audio_3_small_sfx.safetensors (or _music where noted), CLIPLoader t5gemma_b_b_ul2.safetensors type stable_audio, EmptyLatentAudio <seconds> x <batch>, KSampler lcm / simple, 8 steps, cfg 1, denoise 1, VAEDecodeAudio, SaveAudio (flac). 'seed S batch B item i' is item i of one batch of B from seed S. No third-party recordings or libraries were used.
local.default_negative: music, melody, singing, speech, voices, synthesizer, electronic tones, distortion, low quality
local.selection: 16-32 candidates per prompt, 40-190 per slot. Kept by (1) a blind CLAP critic, laion/larger_clap_general: score = similarity to a description of the real event minus the best of 'a synthesized electronic sound effect from a video game', 'music', 'digital beeps and tones', 'static noise'; every shipped take outscores the game's synthesized fallback rendered offline from src/audio.js (womp, birdie_jingle, bad judged on 'a recording of real <instrument> played by a musician' vs synthesizer / chiptune / music box), and the whoosh and landing pools are the critic's top four of the original Veo takes plus new ones; (2) spectrograms: impact first, steel ring 2-9 kHz with a ~1 s decaying rattle and tray clank for chains, woody knock under 1 kHz for trees, no music beds or voices, no clipping.
local.processing: tools/process-sfx.py on each kept candidate: cut from 5 ms before the onset (first sample within 26 dB of the peak; 40 dB for the gradual whoosh, roll, leaves, ohh, applause, womp and jingle) to 60 ms past the last 20 ms window within 42 dB of the loudest, 45 Hz high-pass, 6 ms fade in, 90 ms fade out, mono 44.1 kHz 96 kbps MP3, peak -7 dBFS, or lower so the loudest 300 ms sits at the level its neighbours imply: click -18 dBFS peak, applause about -31 dBFS short-term RMS, the gallery ohh -29, womp -24, birdie jingle -22, bad -28, roll -30, leaves and chains_soft by the same rule. Each take is python tools/process-sfx.py <slot> <candidate flac> --peak P --at A-B --first <take number>, with the exact --peak and --at values listed below.
local.voices: Gallery voices ('Nice shot!', 'Yeah!', 'Oh no!', 'Aww!') were made with Qwen3-TTS 1.7B VoiceDesign (local, C:\ComfyUI\models\qwen3-tts\VoiceDesign, five designed spectator voices, words verified with Whisper small.en) and mixed far back (180 Hz - 4.2 kHz, four ground/tree reflections, 0.45 s diffuse tail) into applause and ohh takes. They are not in the manifest: nobody could listen to judge them natural. Audition art/sfx/voice-candidates/*.mp3 (applause_voices_1: Yeah! + Yeah! over seed 1000 item 11; applause_voices_2: Wow! + Yeah! over item 9; ohh_voices_1: Aww! + Oh no! over the ohh item 8) and add any keeper to the applause / ohh list in assets/manifest.json.

ambient.prompt: Quiet wooded park ambience on a calm summer afternoon: gentle wind through pine and birch trees, soft leaf rustle, several songbirds chirping and calling at different distances, no people, no traffic, realistic stereo field recording. Length: 30 seconds
ambient.processing: mono, 45 Hz high-pass, 28 s loop from 1.5 s whose last 2 s are crossfaded (equal power) back over its head so the end runs straight into the start; loudest 300 ms at -32 dBFS (-39 dBFS overall RMS, peak -18.4); mono 96 kbps MP3. src/audio.js loops only the decoded span, so MP3 encoder padding cannot open a gap at the seam.
